description: A plain-language guide to the features currently available in Kade POS. The PDF manual and Ask product help use this same source.

articles.title: Sign in to your shop
articles.summary: The shop account opens Kade on a device. A separate staff PIN identifies the person using the register.
steps: Open Kade and choose Sign In. Enter the shop account email and password.
For a new business, choose Create Account and follow the email confirmation instructions if shown.
Complete first-time business setup, then choose a register and sign in with your staff PIN.
cautions: A staff PIN does not create a separate online account. Keep the shop password private and use each person's own PIN at the till.

articles.title: Recover a forgotten password
articles.summary: Reset the shop account password through the sign-in page. A forgotten staff PIN is changed by an owner or manager under Staff & PINs.
steps: On the sign-in page, choose Forgot password and enter the account email.
Open the recovery link from that email. Choose a new password, type it again and save.
Return to the till and use your staff PIN as usual.
cautions: Opening the recovery email does not finish the password change. Save the new password first.

articles.title: Set up a new business
articles.summary: The five-step setup prepares the shop, register preferences and customer-facing outputs.
steps: Enter the business name and type. Choose the service style and order types you use, such as takeaway or dine-in.
Choose device preferences, register count and whether to use the Kitchen display. Quick kitchen flow uses Paid and Ready; full flow adds Being made. Enable packet scanning if needed.
Choose the customer languages and currency. Add contact details, an optional logo and a four-digit owner PIN.
Finish setup, continue to the till and check Menu items before selling. Starter items, when supplied, need your prices and availability.
cautions: Setup is for a new business. It is not an editor for an existing shop. Current settings are found under Team & setup, Menu items and Recipes.

Staff screens can use English, Tamil or Sinhala. After setup, owners and managers choose App language in Team & setup, under Business profile. Arabic for staff screens is coming soon. Customer receipt and menu languages are configured separately.

articles.title: Find the right screen
articles.summary: Bottom navigation keeps daily work close. Owners and managers also have a business workspace with clear sections.
steps: Use Till to make a sale. Orders opens the current register shift's receipts. Kitchen appears only when the Kitchen display is enabled.
Owners and managers choose Manage for Overview, Close the day, Reports, Products & stock, and Team & setup.
On a phone, open the business workspace's Menu control to reveal its sections. On the till, use Products and Order check to switch between the product grid and the check.
Use the top Leave register icon to return to staff PIN selection. Use the Sign out of this shop icon to end the device account session.
cautions: Manage and Ask are for owners and managers with the required signed-in access. A service staff PIN does not reveal manager reports.

articles.title: Use the business overview and section menus
articles.summary: Overview brings together the day's activity and shortcuts. Reports and Products & stock are menus that lead to the detailed pages.
steps: Open Manage to see the business Overview and its current sales, stock and cash information.
Choose Reports for Sales report, Daily report, Cash history, Team performance or Waste report.
Choose Products & stock for Menu items, Stock & suppliers or Recipes. Choose Team & setup for people, registers and business settings.
cautions: Use the detailed report for the dates and explanation behind a summary figure.

articles.title: Open the report you need
articles.summary: Reports groups sales, a full day, drawer counts, individual people and waste in one place.
steps: Open Manage, then Reports.
Choose Sales report for trends and item performance, Daily report for a day including cash movements, or Cash history for closed drawer counts.
Choose Team performance for a person's shifts or Waste report for waste and items given away.

articles.title: Find products, stock and recipes
articles.summary: Products & stock separates the products you sell from the supplies you count.
steps: Open Manage, then Products & stock.
Choose Menu items to manage product names, selling prices, custom options and availability.
Choose Stock & suppliers for ingredient counts and suppliers. Choose Recipes to link counted ingredients to products.
cautions: A selling product and a counted stock item are separate records. Adding one does not automatically create the other.

articles.title: Start a register shift
articles.summary: Choose the physical register, identify the cashier and record the cash already in its drawer.
steps: Open Till and choose the register assigned to this device.
Select your staff profile and enter your four-digit PIN. The app checks the PIN after the fourth digit.
Count the physical opening cash. Check the suggested cash float and enter the actual amount, including zero when appropriate.
Choose Start Shift. If another person has an open shift on that register, have it closed before starting a new one.
cautions: One physical register has one open shift. Signing in as a different person does not transfer ownership of that shift.

articles.title: Leave, sign out or close: which one?
articles.summary: Leave register changes who is using the device. Sign out of this shop ends the account session. Close register counts cash and finishes the shift.
steps: For a break, use Leave register. The device returns to staff PIN selection; the open shift stays open.
To end the shop account session on this device, use Sign out of this shop. Another account sign-in is needed to return.
At a shift change or at closing, use Close register, count the cash and get owner or manager PIN approval. Wait for the saved close summary.
cautions: Leaving or signing out does not close a shift or save a drawer count. Finish or park your current check before leaving.

articles.title: Add products to a check
articles.summary: Tap a product card once to add one. Repeated taps add more of the same plain product.
steps: Search for a product or choose its category, then tap the product card.
If the product has no custom options, it goes straight to the check. Tap again to add another.
Review the Order check. Use its quantity controls to increase or decrease a line, or its remove control to remove that line.
On a phone, choose Order check to review the sale, then Products to return to the grid.
cautions: An unavailable product cannot be added to a sale. Check item availability under Menu items or the kitchen availability panel.

articles.title: Choose sizes and custom options
articles.summary: Products with configured options open a selection card before they are added to the check.
steps: Tap the product. Choose the size, milk, toppings or other options shown.
Fill every required group. A group can limit how many options may be chosen.
Check the price on Add to Order, then choose it. The check shows your choices and the total including any extra charges.
Choose Cancel to leave the card without adding the product. Owners and managers configure these groups under Menu items.
cautions: The app waits for product options before allowing payment. If options cannot load, retry instead of assuming the product has none.

articles.title: Record a payment and finish the sale
articles.summary: Take Payment saves the order with its payment method. Kade records cash or card; it does not charge a card or move money.
steps: Review products, quantities, custom choices and the total in the check.
Choose the order type and payment method shown for your shop. Take the customer's cash or complete payment on your separate card terminal.
Choose Take Payment once and wait for the result. When Kitchen display is on, the paid order goes to the kitchen; when off, it finishes at checkout.
After confirmation, use Print receipt to open the receipt preview.
cautions: Cash/card is a recording choice, not integrated payment processing. Handle any actual charge or returned money through your usual payment method.
If the app reports a saved order waiting to send, it has not yet confirmed the order in the cloud. See the connection guidance before entering it again.

articles.title: Scan a packet or type its barcode
articles.summary: Scanning adds products already in your shop's list. For a new barcode, add and check the product details yourself.
steps: If scanning is absent, ask an owner or manager to enable Scan packets at the till under Menu items.
Choose Use camera and allow camera access, or choose Type barcode and enter the number on the packet.
A known, available product follows the normal add-to-check flow, including custom options if configured.
For an unknown number, choose Add this product. Check any public-list suggestion, enter the name, category and your selling price, then save. The new product is added to the check.
cautions: Camera access needs a supported browser and permission. Type barcode is the alternative when the camera cannot scan.
Public product details and photos can be missing or wrong. A match never decides your selling price; check the product and set the price yourself.
Your role must have permission to create products. If saving is refused, ask an owner or manager to add it under Menu items.

articles.title: Save a check for later
articles.summary: Park a check before payment, then resume it from Parked Orders during the same register shift.
steps: With products in the check, choose its Save this order for later control.
The check is saved and cleared so you can serve another customer.
Choose Parked Orders on the till and Resume the required order. Check its products and prices before taking payment.
Delete a parked order only when you no longer need it; confirm the deletion prompt.
cautions: Parking is not taking payment and does not send the check to the kitchen. Parked Orders is scoped to the current register shift and needs a connection to save or load.

articles.title: Find, print or save a receipt
articles.summary: Orders opens Receipt History for the current register shift. Receipts preserve the prices stored on the sale.
steps: Choose Orders in the bottom navigation, or Till functions followed by Orders & receipts.
Find the sale by order number, payment method or order type. Choose View / Reprint.
Review the receipt, then choose Print / Save as PDF. Use the browser's print dialog to select a printer or Save as PDF.
Receipts show the configured customer languages. Use the manager Sales report for older sales beyond the current shift's receipt list.
cautions: Printing uses the browser and the device's printer setup. Kade does not guarantee automatic receipt-printer or cash-drawer hardware control.
The current Receipt History is a shift list, not an all-time receipt archive.

articles.title: Refund or void a sale
articles.summary: A refund records returned money. A void cancels a sale. Both need an owner or manager approval PIN and a reason.
steps: Open Orders, find the sale and choose Refund or Void.
Have an owner or manager enter their four-digit approval PIN.
For a refund, enter the amount, up to the sale total. Enter a clear reason and submit the correction.
Wait for confirmation and check the sale's Refunded or Voided label. Return money through the original payment method separately.
cautions: The app records the correction; it does not send money to a card or bank account.
Refund and Void controls disappear after the sale has an adjustment. Do not assume multiple separate refunds are supported on the same sale.
Do not use the kitchen Cancel order control as a substitute for recording returned money.

articles.title: Turn Kitchen display on or off
articles.summary: An owner or manager can switch Kitchen display under Team & setup, in Business profile. It saves as soon as the change succeeds.
steps: Open Manage, choose Team & setup and find Business profile.
Use the Kitchen display switch. Wait for Kitchen display is on or Kitchen display is off.
When off, Kitchen disappears from navigation and direct kitchen access is blocked. New paid orders finish at checkout, while receipts and sales reports continue.
Turn it on again to restore Kitchen navigation and access. Existing kitchen tickets remain saved and return.
cautions: Turning Kitchen display off does not cancel, finish or delete earlier kitchen tickets. Review any earlier tickets when re-enabling it.
Wait for the saved status. If saving fails, the previous setting remains in effect. Other devices need a connection to receive the change.

articles.title: Move a kitchen ticket through service
articles.summary: Kitchen shows paid orders and their custom choices. The flow depends on the kitchen mode chosen for the business.
steps: Open Kitchen and use its active tickets view. Read the order number, quantities and custom options before preparing it.
In quick flow, move a ticket from Paid to Ready. In full flow, choose Start cooking, then Done cooking to move it through New, Being made and Ready.
Choose Serve order when the order is handed over. This completes the order and removes it from the active queue.
Use Today's Log to review the day's tickets. Use Cancel order only for an order that should be cancelled and confirm the prompt.
cautions: Sales totals count completed orders. A paid ticket still waiting in Kitchen is not counted as completed sales yet.
Cancelling a kitchen ticket excludes that cancelled order from sales, but does not process a money refund. Use the till refund workflow when returning money.
Kitchen requires a connection for live tickets and status changes.

articles.title: Mark an item unavailable or log waste
articles.summary: Availability controls what can be sold. A waste or comp log records products thrown away or given away.
steps: In Kitchen, choose Manage Availability and find the item in Item Availability. Switch it out of stock to stop staff adding it to new sales; restore it when available.
To log waste or an item given away, open Till functions and choose Log waste.
Choose the product, quantity and reason, such as spoilage, on the house, training, complaint or staff meal. Add the person's name if useful, then Save Log.
Owners and managers review these entries in Waste report.
cautions: A waste log is not a paid sale, refund or stock count. Continue physical stock counts; do not assume every waste entry automatically subtracts an ingredient.

articles.title: Record cash added, cash taken out and No Sale
articles.summary: Use Till functions to explain cash movements that are not customer sales.
steps: For money put into the drawer, choose Paid-In. For money removed, choose Paid-Out.
Enter a positive amount and a clear reason, then choose Save Petty Cash. Record each movement when it happens.
Use No Sale to record opening the drawer without a sale.
Review cash movements in the Daily report. For a mistaken paid-in or paid-out entry, use its approved Undo or Fix amount workflow there.
cautions: No Sale logs a drawer opening. It is not a hardware promise that a connected drawer will open automatically.
Paid-In and Paid-Out affect expected drawer cash; they are not product sales.

articles.title: Count cash and close a register
articles.summary: Close register saves the drawer count and finishes that register's shift after owner or manager approval.
steps: Finish current sales and let any saved orders waiting to send clear. On the till choose Close register, or Till functions then Close shift.
Count all physical cash in the drawer, including its opening float. Enter the counted total and choose Continue.
Have an owner or manager enter the four-digit approval PIN. Wait for Shift Closed Successfully.
Review expected cash, counted cash, over or short and cash to bank. Leave the stated cash float in the drawer, then choose Done & Log Out.
cautions: Counted cash is entered before the expected amount is shown. Count the actual drawer, rather than copying an expected number.
A close is complete only after the saved success summary. If it fails, keep the shift open and retry when connected.

articles.title: Finish the business day
articles.summary: Close the day guides the manager through separate register closes and the final daily report.
steps: Open Manage then Close the day. Refresh registers to see which shifts are still open.
For the current register, choose Close this register. For another register, use its assigned device and complete the same cash-count and approval flow.
Check that all required shifts have closed. Open the Daily report for the correct day and review sales, cash counts and exceptions.
Use Print / Save as PDF to save a copy. Open Cash history if a closed drawer count needs checking.
cautions: This screen guides individual shift closes; it does not lock the business date. A later shift or correction can change a report.
Open shifts are not included in closed-shift cash counts. Save the final report after the required register closes.

articles.title: Read a sales report and its graphs
articles.summary: Sales report shows trends, payment and order-type splits, best-selling items and individual orders for chosen dates.
steps: Open Manage, Reports, Sales report. Choose a date shortcut or enter From and To dates, then Apply dates.
Read Gross sales, Completed orders, Average order, Refunds in this period and Net after refunds, then review the trend and split graphs.
Use Best-selling items to compare quantities and item sales. Search Order details by number, status or type and use its page controls.
Use Print / Save as PDF for the full report. Open Download CSV and choose the breakdown you need.
cautions: Only completed orders contribute to sales totals; Order details also shows other statuses. Sales are grouped by the order's recorded date, and refunds by when the refund was recorded.
Net after refunds is gross sales less refunds recorded in the chosen period. It is not profit and can include refunds of earlier sales.
Dates use this device's local calendar and include both selected days. Today is still in progress. The comparison uses the same number of days immediately before the range; choose up to one year.

articles.title: Review the full daily report
articles.summary: Daily report brings together completed sales, payment types, closed shifts, refunds, voids and cash movements for one day.
steps: Open Manage, Reports, Daily report and choose Report date.
Review the sales summary and splits, then the closed-shift reconciliation table.
Read refunds, voids and cash added or taken out. Check reasons and any corrected or undone entries.
Use Print / Save as PDF to save the report after reviewing the day's register closes.
cautions: Sales and cash movements use their recorded times. A shift appears in the day's cash reconciliation when it was closed, even if it opened on an earlier day.
The day uses the device's local calendar. Keep register devices on the shop's intended time zone to compare dates consistently.

articles.title: Check or correct a closed drawer count
articles.summary: Cash history compares expected and counted cash for closed shifts and keeps approved corrections with their reasons.
steps: Open Manage, Reports, Cash history. Set From and To dates and find the register and staff member.
Compare opening float, expected cash, counted cash, over or short, cash to bank and the close approver.
For a counting mistake, choose Fix count. Enter the corrected counted amount, give the reason and enter an owner or manager approval PIN.
Review the updated count. Open Corrected to see the original value, correction and approver.
cautions: Expected cash starts with opening float, adds cash sales and paid-in money, then subtracts cash refunds and paid-out money. Card payments are not drawer cash.
Fix count corrects a saved count; it does not reopen a shift or erase the earlier record. Older records may show a dash where information was not captured.

articles.title: Undo a mistaken cash entry or fix its amount
articles.summary: A mistaken paid-in or paid-out entry is corrected in the Daily report, with a reason and approval.
steps: Open Daily report and select the day containing the paid-in or paid-out entry.
Choose Undo if the entry should not exist, or Fix amount if the cash movement happened with a different amount.
Enter the new amount when asked, explain the correction and enter an owner or manager approval PIN.
Review the updated cash figures and the original entry marked Undone or replaced.
cautions: Corrections keep the earlier record and reason. Correct the record that is wrong; do not create an opposite cash movement just to hide a mistake.

articles.title: Review one person's shifts
articles.summary: Team performance shows each person's sales and shift accountability across chosen dates.
steps: Open Manage, Reports, Team performance, or use Individual staff performance under Team & setup.
Choose From and To dates. Find the person and expand their card to see individual shifts.
Review completed sales, order counts, drawer openings and the expected/count/banked figures available for each shift.
Read refunds approved and voids approved as approvals by that person, rather than sales they originally rang up.
cautions: Open shifts do not yet have final drawer counts. This is a shift accountability report, not a payroll or dedicated attendance system.

articles.title: Review waste and items given away
articles.summary: Waste report shows recent waste and comp entries, reasons, quantities and approximate value.
steps: Open Manage, Reports, Waste report.
Review the recent seven-day summary and most common reason.
Read each recent event for its product, quantity, reason, time and person when recorded.
Use the patterns to improve ordering or staff training, and recount ingredients where needed.
cautions: Waste value uses current menu prices. It is an approximation, not historical ingredient cost or profit loss.

articles.title: Add or edit selling products
articles.summary: Menu items manages the product list used by the till and the customer menu.
steps: Open Manage, Products & stock, Menu items. Choose Add product or edit an existing item.
Enter the product name, category and selling price. Fill translated names for the customer languages in use.
If scanning is enabled, add the barcode and optional packet details. Check any public-list lookup before saving.
Use search and the active/available filters to find an item. Set availability for a temporary sell-out; use the menu's active controls when the item should be removed from the current menu.
cautions: Availability and active menu status are separate. A sold-out item can stay on your managed list while being unavailable for new sales.
Earlier sale prices remain stored with the sale. A product's name in some reports comes from the current menu.

articles.title: Set up sizes, extras and required choices
articles.summary: Use a saved product's Modifiers tab to configure choices shown when staff tap that product.
steps: Open or save the product first, then choose its Modifiers tab.
Add a group, such as Size or Milk, and decide whether a choice is required.
Add the options and each option's extra cost. Include translated option names where useful.
Open the product on the till and check its selection card and resulting price before using it for customer sales.
cautions: Custom choices only appear for products with configured groups. Deleting a group or option changes the choices available for future sales.

articles.title: Show or print the customer menu
articles.summary: The customer menu is a clean display of product names, categories and base prices in the configured languages.
steps: Open the customer menu on a signed-in shop device.
Choose a language shown in the menu controls to display the corresponding names.
Use Print / Save as PDF to make a menu copy through the browser's print dialog.
Choose its back control to return to the till. Update products and translated names under Menu items.
cautions: This route requires shop sign-in; it is not a public ordering or QR-ordering service. Custom choices are intentionally omitted from the menu's base-price display.

articles.title: Count stock and add supplier details
articles.summary: Stock & suppliers holds ingredients and supplies, physical counts, low-stock levels and supplier details.
steps: Open Manage, Products & stock, Stock & suppliers and choose Add Item.
Enter the name and unit, such as litres, kilograms or pieces. Select a supplier or add one with its contact number and lead time.
Set the minimum warning level and usual full amount if useful. These help identify Running low or Getting low items.
Choose Count on an item and enter the total quantity you physically have now, not the amount just delivered. Add the counter's name if useful, then Save Stock Count.
cautions: A stock count replaces the recorded quantity with the current physical total. Keep units consistent across counts and recipes.
If a notice says sales usage did not match stock, recount the ingredient. Stock is not silently driven below zero.
A supplier contact link opens your messaging app; you still choose and send any message yourself.

articles.title: Link recipes to stock counts
articles.summary: Optional recipe tracking subtracts linked ingredient quantities when an order completes.
steps: Create and count ingredients in Stock & suppliers first.
Open Recipes and turn on Track ingredients automatically if your shop wants this behavior.
Expand a product, choose an ingredient and enter the quantity used per one product in the ingredient's stored unit. Add the link and repeat for other ingredients.
Check recipe quantities carefully and continue physical stock counts. Turn the switch off when you want to stop automatic ingredient tracking.
cautions: Products without a recipe do not change ingredient stock automatically. With Kitchen display on, usage is recorded when an order completes; with it off, the paid order completes at checkout.
Turning recipe tracking off keeps existing recipe links but stops automatic tracking. This is not ingredient costing or full accounting.

articles.title: Change the app language
articles.summary: An owner or manager can choose English, Tamil or Sinhala for the staff screens across this shop. Arabic is shown as Coming soon and cannot be selected yet.
steps: Open Manage, choose Team & setup, then find App language in Business profile. The App language link from Ask opens this setting directly.
Choose English, Tamil or Sinhala and select Save language. The screen changes after the setting is saved and its translations have loaded.
This shop setting applies to the till, order controls, Kitchen display, manager pages and Ask controls. Other signed-in devices refresh the setting automatically; reopening the app also reads it.
Ask uses the selected app language for its answers unless you request another language. Ask can explain the setting and link to it; you choose and save the language yourself.
To return to English, choose English in the same setting and save. English stays visible alongside each language name to help you find it.
cautions: Only an owner or manager can save the shop language. It does not change prices, order records, staff PINs, currency or the shop name.
Customer receipt and menu languages are separate. Product names use the saved translated name where available and otherwise keep their original name. Enter translated names under Menu items.
Arabic for staff screens is coming soon. Existing customer Arabic names and receipt/menu support remain separate from this setting.
An internet connection is needed to save the setting and load a language for the first time. If translations do not load, choose Try again. Saved orders and your order check are kept.

articles.title: Manage people and staff PINs
articles.summary: Staff & PINs manages register identities, service staff or manager roles and four-digit PINs.
steps: Open Manage, Team & setup, Staff & PINs. Choose Add Staff to create a new profile.
Enter the name, choose Service Staff or Manager (SIC) as appropriate and set the required four-digit PIN.
Use Edit to update a profile or reset a PIN. Leave the PIN blank when editing to keep the existing one.
Use Remove only when a person should no longer sign in and the app permits removal. The owner profile cannot be removed here.
cautions: A PIN profile does not create a new email account, invite a business member or grant a separate online login. The page can refuse account-linked role changes.
A person with active shifts or referenced history may not be removable. Keep approval PINs private and do not share one person's identity across staff.

articles.title: Name registers and set their cash float
articles.summary: Registers & cash float manages physical checkout names and the usual cash to leave for the next shift.
steps: Open Manage, Team & setup, Registers & cash float.
Choose Add Register or Edit an existing register. Use a clear, unique name that staff recognize.
Set a cash float of zero or more and save. It becomes the suggested opening amount for a new shift and helps calculate cash to bank at close.
At each opening, the cashier still counts and enters the actual cash rather than assuming the suggested float is correct.
cautions: A float is cash left in the drawer, not a sale or paid-in event. Do not remove a register with an open shift or needed history; check the app's refusal or confirmation carefully.

articles.title: Find business settings and access rules
articles.summary: Team & setup shows business details and connects you to staff, registers, performance and supplier settings.
steps: Open Manage and Team & setup.
Use Staff & PINs for a person, Registers & cash float for a checkout point, or Individual staff performance for their shifts.
Find Business profile to review the name, currency and business type, and to change Kitchen display.
For scanning, open Menu items. For automatic ingredient tracking, open Recipes.
cautions: Name, currency and business type are displayed here; the current Business profile screen edits the Kitchen display switch. It is not a full business-details editor.
Owners and managers can view the business workspace. Service staff use the till and kitchen rather than manager reports.

articles.title: Ask for help or a business explanation
articles.summary: Ask helps authorized owners and managers understand their business data and find the right product feature.
steps: Open a manager page and choose Ask. Start a new chat for a new topic, or use Chat history to return to an earlier conversation.
For product help, ask a clear question such as How do I turn off the kitchen?, Where can I correct a cash count?, or What is the difference between leaving and closing a register?.
For business questions, give the period and what you want to know. On a report page, Ask can use the report being viewed and show useful report links or visual summaries.
Open the suggested page link and follow the steps there. Check the dates, units and report definitions before making a business decision.
cautions: Ask requires a connection and the correct owner or manager account and PIN access. It is not available to an ordinary service staff session.
Ask can explain and link to a feature; required approval and settings changes still happen in their screens. Never put passwords, PINs or payment-card details into chat.

articles.title: Prepare a purchase-order draft in Ask
articles.summary: Ask can prepare a supplier order draft for you to review in chat. It does not place an order with the supplier.
steps: Open Ask as an authorized owner or manager. Tell it which supplier, products and quantities you want in the draft, or ask it to help review low stock.
Read the draft card in the chat. Check supplier details, units, quantities and notes against your actual stock.
Make the purchasing decision yourself and contact the supplier through your usual process. Keep your own sent-order and delivery records.
After a delivery, count the physical total in Stock & suppliers and record the new stock count.
cautions: The draft is saved with the chat for review. It does not save a purchase order in POS stock records, email a supplier, submit an order or receive stock automatically.
The current Stock & suppliers screen manages items, supplier details and counts. It does not expose a separate saved purchase-order workflow.

articles.title: Enable Offline protection
articles.summary: An owner or manager can enable till continuity for short internet interruptions. The setting prepares each online, open register; Ready means that device has saved the complete products and custom choices.
steps: Connect to the internet and open Team & setup, then Business profile.
Turn Offline protection On and wait for the saved confirmation. The setting is shared by the shop, but preparation happens separately on each open register.
Return to the till and wait for Ready. If preparation fails, keep using the connected till and choose Prepare again. The device is not protected until Ready appears.
To turn it off, return to the same setting while connected. Previously saved sales remain on the device and continue to sync.
cautions: Only an owner or manager can change this shop setting. Keep each prepared till open during an outage; app reopening and new sign-in still need internet.
Protection covers the till and its locally saved receipts. Kitchen tickets, reports and Ask catch up after reconnection.
Each sale retains its original account, shop, register session, price and time. A matching confirmed upload is required before it leaves the waiting list.

articles.title: Keep serving during a connection interruption
articles.summary: Enable Offline protection while online, then prepare each open register. A Ready till keeps recording known products, their options and receipts on that device; sales send automatically when internet returns.
steps: While connected, an owner or manager opens Team & setup, Business profile and turns on Offline protection.
Open the register and wait for Offline protection: Ready on that device. Preparation saves a complete set of products and custom choices. Repeat this on each device you use.

Keep that till open if the internet drops. Ring known items, choose their prepared options and take payment as usual. Each sale is saved on this device before the check clears, with a local receipt reference.
If a connected till says a sale has not been confirmed, choose Retry saved sale before starting another check. It reuses the same sale reference; do not take payment again or re-enter the items.
Use Saved sales to view waiting receipts. When the connection returns, the same sales send automatically with their original sale time. Kitchen tickets and reports update after confirmation.
Wait for the saved-sales count to clear before closing the register. If a sale needs review, keep the device and ask a manager to check it; do not ring it again.
cautions: First opening the app, signing in and opening a register need internet. Keep the prepared till open during the interruption; offline refresh or reopening is not supported.
New or unknown barcode products, parking checks, refunds, void approvals, staff PIN changes, drawer actions and register closing need internet. Kitchen, reports and Ask also need internet.

Saved sales belong to this account, shop, register session and browser on this device. Do not clear browser site data, reset local app state, switch browser profiles or discard the device before they sync.
If a register was closed on another device, an unsent sale stays saved for review. It does not silently alter the closed shift. Turning protection off also keeps previously saved sales.
A power cut requires a device with battery power or another power supply. Kade records the payment method; whether a card terminal can take payments without internet depends on that terminal.
